title: Finding 1: Target Class Imbalance & Prevalence Profile
question: What is the baseline prevalence of heart disease in the audited patient cohort?
analysis: Frequency distribution analysis across 9,000 raw patient records.
result: Target prevalence is 30.30% positive cases (2,727 disease patients vs 6,273 healthy controls).
interpretation: The dataset presents moderate class imbalance. Relying solely on raw Accuracy produces inflated optimistic baseline scores.
dm_implication: Evaluation metrics must emphasize Weighted F1-score, Recall/Sensitivity, and ROC-AUC under Stratified 5-Fold Cross-Validation.

title: Finding 2: Chronotropic Response Deficit (Max Heart Rate Achieved)
question: Does peak exercise heart rate differ significantly between healthy individuals and heart disease patients?
analysis: Mann-Whitney U non-parametric hypothesis test and Cohen's d effect size calculation.
interpretation: Patients with heart disease exhibit severely blunted peak heart rate during stress testing (mean 145 bpm vs 173 bpm).
dm_implication: Max Heart Rate Achieved is the single strongest negative correlation predictor (-0.58 Pearson correlation) in the classification pipeline.

title: Finding 3: ST Depression & Myocardial Ischemia Marker
question: Is electrocardiogram ST segment depression significantly elevated in diseased patients?
analysis: Mann-Whitney U test and Glass Rank-Biserial Correlation.
interpretation: ST depression (exercise-induced ischemia marker) is significantly elevated in heart disease patients (mean 1.62 mm vs 0.75 mm).
dm_implication: Serves as the top positive clinical feature across Decision Trees, Random Forest Gini importance, and Permutation importance.

title: Finding 4: Superior Margin-Based Discrimination (SVM Classifier)
question: Which supervised classification algorithm achieves optimal risk prediction accuracy and generalization?
analysis: Stratified 5-Fold Cross-Validation GridSearch benchmarking across 6 algorithms.
result: Support Vector Machine (RBF kernel) achieved 89.17% Accuracy, 0.8898 Weighted F1, and 0.9422 ROC-AUC.
interpretation: RBF Support Vector Machine maps non-linear biomarker interactions into high-dimensional hyperplanes with optimal margin separation.
dm_implication: Selected as the core prediction engine deployed in the Streamlit web dashboard.

title: Finding 5: Synergistic Risk Triad (Age, LDL Cholesterol, HbA1c)
question: Do metabolic blood biomarkers interact synergistically with demographic age?
analysis: Spearman rank correlations and multi-perspective consensus feature ranking.
result: Age, LDL Cholesterol, and HbA1c all display statistically significant positive correlations (p < 0.0001).
interpretation: Elevated metabolic biomarkers combined with advancing age compounded overall cardiovascular vulnerability.
dm_implication: Feature engineering ratios (Cholesterol/HDL Ratio, Pulse Pressure) successfully capture non-linear metabolic risk.
